+"""Direct SM80 rounded-SwiGLU qualification; does not change the runtime gate.
+
+Run on A100 from the repo root with the existing CUDA/Torch environment::
+
+    PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest -q -s \
+        test/registered/kernels/ops/activation/test_swiglu_rounding_sm80.py
+    PYTHONPATH=python python \
+        test/registered/kernels/ops/activation/test_swiglu_rounding_sm80.py --benchmark
+
+Shapes below are full [tokens, gate+up] input shapes. Finite outputs must
+match bits (including signed zero); NaN payload/sign are not a contract, but
+NaN locations and infinity signs must match. No tolerance silently accepts ULP
+differences. Non-finite inputs are tested separately from normal finite inputs.
+The benchmark runs only after correctness passes; both paths include activation
+rounding, optional clamping, and the final write to a caller-provided output.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import statistics
+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+
+INPUT_SHAPES = [(6, 640), (6, 576), (1, 5120)]
+DTYPES = [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16]
+LIMITS = [0.0, 10.0]
+
+
+def _require_sm80():
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.version.hip is not None:
+        pytest.skip("requires NVIDIA CUDA SM80")
+    capability = torch.cuda.get_device_capability()
+    if capability != (8, 0):
+        pytest.skip(f"requires actual SM80, got {capability}")
+    return capability
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
+def require_actual_sm80():
+    _require_sm80()
+
+
+def _fused(x, out=None, *, clamp_limit=0.0):
+    # Import only after checking the real device. Deliberately bypass the
+    # SM90-only swiglu_limit_func wrapper, not its rounding semantics.
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.activation.activation import (
+        silu_and_mul_with_activation_rounding,
+    )
+
+    return silu_and_mul_with_activation_rounding(x, out, clamp_limit=clamp_limit)
+
+
+def _torch_chain(x, out=None, *, clamp_limit=0.0):
+    gate, up = x.chunk(2, dim=-1)
+    if clamp_limit > 0:
+        gate = gate.clamp(max=clamp_limit)
+        up = up.clamp(min=-clamp_limit, max=clamp_limit)
+    # Do NOT promote to float or fuse this expression: eager F.silu writes a
+    # BF16/FP16 intermediate before the multiplication, as the runtime does.
+    value = F.silu(gate) * up
+    if out is None:
+        return value
+    out.copy_(value)
+    return out
+
+
+def _bits(x):
+    return x.contiguous().view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32) & 0xFFFF
+
+
+def _ordered_bits(x):
+    bits = _bits(x)
+    return torch.where((bits & 0x8000) != 0, 0xFFFF - bits, bits + 0x8000)
+
+
+def _assert_exact(actual, expected, label):
+    assert actual.shape == expected.shape and actual.dtype == expected.dtype
+    both_nan = torch.isnan(actual) & torch.isnan(expected)
+    mismatch = (_bits(actual) != _bits(expected)) & ~both_nan
+    count = int(mismatch.sum().item())
+    if not count:
+        return
+    finite = torch.isfinite(actual) & torch.isfinite(expected)
+    ulps = (_ordered_bits(actual) - _ordered_bits(expected)).abs()
+    max_ulp = int(ulps[finite].max().item()) if bool(finite.any()) else None
+    first = mismatch.nonzero()[0].tolist()
+    index = tuple(first)
+    pytest.fail(
+        f"{label}: bit mismatches={count}/{actual.numel()}, "
+        f"max_finite_ULP={max_ulp}, first_index={first}, "
+        f"actual={actual[index].item()}, expected={expected[index].item()}, "
+        f"actual_bits=0x{int(_bits(actual)[index]):04x}, "
+        f"expected_bits=0x{int(_bits(expected)[index]):04x}; "
+        "NaN payload/sign excluded, signed zero included"
+    )
+
+
+def _input(shape, dtype, case):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(20260416)
+    if case == "random":
+        return torch.randn(shape, dtype=dtype, device="cuda", generator=generator) * 12
+    finfo = torch.finfo(dtype)
+    values = torch.tensor(
+        [-finfo.max, -1000, -100, -90, -20, -10, -1, -finfo.tiny,
+         -0.0, 0.0, finfo.tiny, 1, 10, 20, 90, 100, 1000, finfo.max],
+        dtype=dtype, device="cuda",
+    )
+    if case == "boundary":
+        centers = torch.tensor([-10.0, 0.0, 10.0], dtype=dtype, device="cuda")
+        values = torch.cat(
+            [torch.nextafter(centers, torch.full_like(centers, -float("inf"))),
+             centers,
+             torch.nextafter(centers, torch.full_like(centers, float("inf")))]
+        )
+    rows, width = shape
+    n = rows * (width // 2)
+    indices = torch.arange(n, device="cuda")
+    # Different coprime walks expose every gate/up extreme combination rather
+    # than coupling large gates only to large up values.
+    gate = values[indices % values.numel()].view(rows, width // 2)
+    up = values[(indices // values.numel() + indices * 5 + 1) % values.numel()]
+    return torch.cat((gate, up.view_as(gate)), dim=-1).contiguous()
+
+
+def test_gpu_capability():
+    assert _require_sm80() == (8, 0)
+    print(f"device={torch.cuda.get_device_name()} capability=(8, 0) "
+          f"torch={torch.__version__} cuda={torch.version.cuda}")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", INPUT_SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("limit", LIMITS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("case", ["random", "extreme", "boundary"])
+def test_swiglu_finite_exact(shape, dtype, limit, case):
+    x = _input(shape, dtype, case)
+    original = x.clone()
+    expected = _torch_chain(x, clamp_limit=limit)
+    label = f"shape={shape} {dtype} limit={limit} {case}"
+    _assert_exact(_fused(x, clamp_limit=limit), expected, label + " allocated")
+    out = torch.empty_like(expected)
+    assert _fused(x, out, clamp_limit=limit) is out
+    _assert_exact(out, expected, label + " out")
+    assert torch.equal(_bits(x), _bits(original)), "input unexpectedly mutated"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("limit", LIMITS)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nonfinite", [False, True], ids=["finite-bits", "nan-inf"])
+def test_swiglu_all_16bit_patterns(dtype, limit, nonfinite):
+    values = torch.arange(65536, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32).to(torch.int16).view(dtype)
+    gate = values.view(-1, 32)
+    up = values.roll(17953).view_as(gate)
+    if not nonfinite:
+        # Preserve all finite encodings, including signed zeros/subnormals.
+        # Non-finites are independently qualified by the nan-inf case.
+        gate = torch.where(torch.isfinite(gate), gate, torch.ones_like(gate))
+        up = torch.where(torch.isfinite(up), up, torch.ones_like(up))
+    x = torch.cat((gate, up), dim=-1)
+    _assert_exact(
+        _fused(x, clamp_limit=limit), _torch_chain(x, clamp_limit=limit),
+        f"all patterns {dtype} limit={limit} nonfinite={nonfinite}",
+    )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", INPUT_SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("limit", LIMITS)
+def test_swiglu_cuda_graph(shape, dtype, limit):
+    x = _input(shape, dtype, "random")
+    out = _fused(x, clamp_limit=limit)  # JIT and warmup before capture.
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            _fused(x, out, clamp_limit=limit)
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        _fused(x, out, clamp_limit=limit)
+    for _ in range(2):
+        x.neg_()  # Replay must read current storage, not captured constants.
+        graph.replay()
+        _assert_exact(out, _torch_chain(x, clamp_limit=limit),
+                      f"graph {shape} {dtype} limit={limit}")
+
+
+def _event_us(fn, iterations, repeats):
+    samples = []
+    for _ in range(repeats):
+        start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+        start.record()
+        for _ in range(iterations):
+            fn()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / iterations)
+    return statistics.median(samples)
+
+
+def benchmark(iterations=200, repeats=7, include_fp16=False):
+    _require_sm80()
+    print(f"device={torch.cuda.get_device_name()} capability={torch.cuda.get_device_capability()} "
+          f"torch={torch.__version__} cuda={torch.version.cuda}")
+    print("All times median CUDA-event us/call; graph = one full chain per replay.")
+    print("input_shape dtype limit mode torch_us fused_us speedup")
+    for dtype in (DTYPES if include_fp16 else [torch.bfloat16]):
+        for shape in INPUT_SHAPES:
+            for limit in LIMITS:
+                x = _input(shape, dtype, "random")
+                reference = _torch_chain(x, clamp_limit=limit)
+                outputs = [torch.empty_like(reference), torch.empty_like(reference)]
+                funcs = [lambda: _torch_chain(x, outputs[0], clamp_limit=limit),
+                         lambda: _fused(x, outputs[1], clamp_limit=limit)]
+                graphs = []
+                for fn, out in zip(funcs, outputs):
+                    for _ in range(10):
+                        fn()
+                    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+                    _assert_exact(out, reference, "benchmark warmup")
+                    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+                    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                        fn()
+                    graph.replay()
+                    _assert_exact(out, reference, "benchmark graph")
+                    graphs.append(graph)
+                for mode, calls in [("events", funcs), ("cudagraph", [g.replay for g in graphs])]:
+                    times = [_event_us(fn, iterations, repeats) for fn in calls]
+                    print(f"{shape} {dtype} {limit:g} {mode} "
+                          f"{times[0]:.4f} {times[1]:.4f} {times[0] / times[1]:.3f}x")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--benchmark", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--include-fp16", action="store_true", help="also benchmark FP16")
+    parser.add_argument("--iterations", type=int, default=200)
+    parser.add_argument("--repeats", type=int, default=7)
+    args, pytest_args = parser.parse_known_args()
+    if args.iterations <= 0 or args.repeats <= 0:
+        parser.error("iterations and repeats must be positive")
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() != (8, 0):
+        print("SKIP: requires an actual NVIDIA SM80 GPU; no benchmark was run")
+        sys.exit(0)
+    status = pytest.main([__file__, "-q", "-s", *pytest_args])
+    if status == 0 and args.benchmark:

+"""SM80 V4.1 real writers -> real paged reader, against CPU-only oracles.
+
+Run directly with unittest on an SM80 GPU. This deliberately does not inherit
+TestV41KVStore (which is gated to SM100/gfx950), or register/change CI gates.
+All FP8 casts in the reference quantizers/dequantizers happen on the CPU.
+Only finite inputs are tested, including both signs of zero; arbitrary NaN
+payloads and hardware-specific NaN canonicalization are outside this contract.
+"""

+import unittest
+
+import torch
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.attn import fused_store_cache
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.dequant_k_cache import (
+    dequantize_k_cache_paged_v41,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.elementwise import (
+    fused_k_norm_rope_flashmla,
+    fused_q_norm_rope,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.kv_layout import KVLayout
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.torch_quant import (
+    dequantize_k_cache_v41,
+    quantize_k_cache_v41,
+)
+from sglang.test.kernels.deepseek_v4.dsv41_kv_quant_reference import (
+    dequantize_k_cache_v41_fp4,
+    quantize_k_cache_v41_fp4,
+)
+
+CASES = {
+    KVLayout.V41: (quantize_k_cache_v41, dequantize_k_cache_v41),
+    KVLayout.V41_FP4: (quantize_k_cache_v41_fp4, dequantize_k_cache_v41_fp4),
+}
+NUM_PAGES = 3
+
+
+def _is_sm80():
+    return (
+        torch.version.hip is None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0)
+    )
+
+
+def _bits(x):
+    """Compare BF16 bits, not values: +0 and -0 are distinct."""
+    assert x.dtype == torch.bfloat16
+    return x.contiguous().view(torch.int16)
+
+
+def _signs(n, heads=None):
+    shape = (n, 512) if heads is None else (n, heads, 512)
+    ids = torch.arange(torch.tensor(shape).prod().item()).reshape(shape)
+    return torch.where((ids + ids // 7) % 3 == 0, -1.0, 1.0).to(torch.bfloat16)

+def _weight():
+    # BF16-exact, varied across tiles and within each tile. No zero entries:
+    # eps=0 on +/-1 gives exactly sign * weight before BF16 rounding.
+    ids = torch.arange(512)
+    return ((1.0 + (ids % 7).float() / 8) * torch.exp2((ids % 9 - 4).float())).to(
+        torch.bfloat16
+    )
+
+
+def _freqs_table(max_pos=13):
+    # Exactly identity or i, avoiding sin/cos and reduction-order tolerances.
+    # Vary by both position and complex pair so passing a table instead of
+    # gathered per-token frequencies to standalone store cannot pass by chance.
+    ids = torch.arange(max_pos)[:, None] + torch.arange(32)[None, :]
+    use_i = ids % 3 == 1
+    return torch.complex((~use_i).float(), use_i.float())
+
+
+def _rope_cpu(x, per_token_freqs):
+    """Independent real-arithmetic RoPE, with explicit BF16 output rounding."""
+    assert x.device.type == per_token_freqs.device.type == "cpu"
+    assert per_token_freqs.shape == (x.shape[0], 32)
+    pairs = x[..., -64:].float().reshape(*x.shape[:-1], 32, 2)
+    shape = (x.shape[0],) + (1,) * (x.ndim - 2) + (32,)
+    c, s = per_token_freqs.real.reshape(shape), per_token_freqs.imag.reshape(shape)
+    a, b = pairs[..., 0], pairs[..., 1]
+    tail = torch.stack((a * c - b * s, b * c + a * s), dim=-1)
+    return torch.cat((x[..., :-64], tail.flatten(-2).to(torch.bfloat16)), dim=-1)

+def _locs(page_size, dtype=torch.int32):

+    # all unique for P=2 as well. One slot/page subset remains unwritten.
+    return torch.tensor(
+        [0, page_size - 1, page_size, 2 * page_size - 1, 3 * page_size - 1],

+def _reference_pages(layout, page_size, locs, values):
+    """CPU quantization, then restore zero-initialized unwritten cache rows."""
+    assert locs.device.type == values.device.type == "cpu"

+    full = torch.zeros(NUM_PAGES, page_size, 512, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    full.view(-1, 512)[locs.long()] = values
+    quant, _ = CASES[layout]

+    written = torch.zeros(NUM_PAGES * page_size, dtype=torch.bool)
+    written[locs.long()] = True
+    written = written.reshape(NUM_PAGES, page_size, 1)
+    # Q(full zeros) has NONZERO scale bytes. Real sparse writes leave their
+    # unwritten footer bytes zero, so merely quantizing full is not an oracle.
+    lo = layout.scale_offset(page_size)
+    hi = lo + page_size * layout.scale_bytes
+    footer = pages[:, lo:hi].reshape(NUM_PAGES, page_size, layout.scale_bytes)
+    footer = footer.masked_fill(~written, 0)
+    pages[:, lo:hi] = footer.reshape(NUM_PAGES, -1)  # explicit footer writeback
+    payload = pages[:, :lo].reshape(NUM_PAGES, page_size, layout.data_bytes)
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(payload.masked_select(~written)) == 0
+    assert torch.count_nonzero(pages[:, hi:]) == 0  # page padding stays zero
+    return pages

+"""Read 4 rows per original expert matrix; verify byte decoding on SM80.
+
+Standalone diagnostic, not CI/model execution. Does not load full tensors or
+write model data. Run with CUDA torch/Triton and --model-dir CHECKPOINT.
+"""
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import pathlib
+import struct
+import sys
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+ROOT=pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
+SOURCE=ROOT/'python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4'
+PACKAGE='sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4'
+for name in ('kv_layout','dequant_k_cache_sm80'):
+    spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(PACKAGE+'.'+name,SOURCE/(name+'.py'))
+    module=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[spec.name]=module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+codec=module
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def decode_rows(P,S,O,N:tl.constexpr,B:tl.constexpr):
+    i=tl.program_id(0)*B+tl.arange(0,B)
+    packed=tl.load(P+i//2,mask=i<N,other=0).to(tl.int32)
+    code=(packed>>((i&1)*4))&15
+    scale=tl.load(S+i//32,mask=i<N,other=127)
+    value=codec._scaled_bf16(codec._e2m1_to_fp32(code),codec._ue8m0_to_fp32(scale))
+    tl.store(O+i,value,mask=i<N)
+
+
+def read_rows(root,index,key,rows=4):
+    with (root/index[key]).open('rb') as f:
+        length=struct.unpack('<Q',f.read(8))[0]
+        meta=json.loads(f.read(length))[key]
+        if len(meta['shape'])!=2:raise ValueError('expected matrix')
+        rows=min(rows,meta['shape'][0]);width=meta['shape'][1]
+        f.seek(8+length+meta['data_offsets'][0])
+        data=f.read(rows*width)
+    if len(data)!=rows*width:raise ValueError('incomplete sample')
+    return torch.frombuffer(bytearray(data),dtype=torch.uint8).reshape(rows,width),meta
+
+
+def main():
+    args=argparse.ArgumentParser();args.add_argument('--model-dir',required=True)
+    root=pathlib.Path(args.parse_args().model_dir)
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()!=(8,0):raise RuntimeError('requires SM80')
+    index=json.loads((root/'model.safetensors.index.json').read_text())['weight_map']
+    lookup=torch.tensor([0.,.5,1.,1.5,2.,3.,4.,6.,-0.,-.5,-1.,-1.5,-2.,-3.,-4.,-6.],dtype=torch.float64)
+    results=[]
+    for matrix in ('w1','w3','w2'):
+        prefix='layers.0.ffn.experts.0.'+matrix
+        packed,wm=read_rows(root,index,prefix+'.weight')
+        scales,sm=read_rows(root,index,prefix+'.scale')
+        if wm['dtype']!='I8' or sm['dtype']!='F8_E8M0':raise ValueError('unexpected format')
+        width=packed.shape[1]*2
+        if width%32 or scales.shape!=(packed.shape[0],width//32):raise ValueError('unexpected scale shape')
+        codes=torch.stack((packed&15,packed>>4),-1).flatten(1).long()
+        ref=(lookup[codes]*scales.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu).float().double().repeat_interleave(32,1)).bfloat16()
+        p=packed.cuda();s=scales.cuda();out=torch.empty_like(ref,device='cuda')
+        decode_rows[(triton.cdiv(out.numel(),256),)](p,s,out,out.numel(),256)
+        cpu=out.cpu();finite=~ref.isnan()
+        assert torch.equal(cpu.isnan(),ref.isnan())
+        assert torch.equal(cpu.view(torch.int16)[finite],ref.view(torch.int16)[finite])
+        # A tiny projection using the sampled actual rows, not a full expert.
+        torch.manual_seed(4111)
+        x=(torch.randn(2,width)*.02).bfloat16()
+        got=x.cuda().float()@out.float().T
+        expected=x.float()@ref.float().T
+        torch.testing.assert_close(got.cpu(),expected,rtol=1e-4,atol=2e-4)
+        results.append({'matrix':matrix,'checkpoint_weight_shape':wm['shape'],'rows_sampled':packed.shape[0],
+                        'payload_bytes':packed.numel()+scales.numel(),'decode_bit_exact':True,
+                        'projection_max_abs':float((got.cpu()-expected).abs().max())})
+    print(json.dumps({'scope':'4 real rows per matrix; software decode and tiny FP32 projection, not full MoE',
+                      'gpu':torch.cuda.get_device_name(),'results':results},indent=2))
+
+if __name__=='__main__':main()

+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)

+    return fallback.dequantize_k_cache_paged_sm80(cache, ids, page, out, layout)
+

+def reference(cache, ids, page, layout):
+    c = cache.cpu()
+    ids = ids.cpu().long()
+    selected = c[ids // page]
+    slots = ids % page
+    data = selected.gather(
+        1, slots[:, None] * layout.data_bytes + torch.arange(layout.data_bytes)
+    )
+    sb = selected.gather(
+        1,
+        layout.scale_offset(page)
+        + slots[:, None] * layout.scale_bytes
+        + torch.arange(layout.scale_bytes),
+    )
+    if layout == KVLayout.V41:
+        values = data.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()
+        scales = sb.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu).float()
+    else:
+        codes = torch.stack((data & 15, data >> 4), -1).flatten(1).long()
+        table = torch.tensor(
+            [0., .5, 1., 1.5, 2., 3., 4., 6., -0., -.5, -1., -1.5, -2., -3., -4., -6.]
+        )
+        values = table[codes]
+        scales = sb.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float()
+    # Float64 avoids FTZ in the reference and represents every operand exactly.
+    result = (values.double() * scales.double().repeat_interleave(layout.tile_size, 1)).bfloat16()
+    return result[:, None, :]

+"""Explicit production BLOCK8/16 precision diagnostics against CPU FP64.
+
+No model/checkpoint/route changes. Run directly on real SM80. Uses the EXISTING
+oracle tolerances (.015/.004 output, 2e-5 LSE), never bitwise agreement between
+FP32 reduction geometries. Metrics are diagnostic, not replacement thresholds.
+"""
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import pathlib
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
+spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
+    "_geometry_precision_tiled_tests", HERE / "test_dsv41_sm80_sparse_tiled.py"
+)
+original = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+spec.loader.exec_module(original)
+base = original.base
+candidate = base.leaf("sparse_attention_sm80_headshared").sparse_attention_sm80_headshared
+KVLayout = base.KVLayout
+
+
+def realistic_cache(layout, page):
+    """Finite moderate scales: no E4M3 NaN or overflow hiding comparisons.
+
+    FP8 payload comes from CPU rounded normal values; scale bytes 124..128
+    represent 1/8..2. FP4 payload has all nibble codes, scale bytes 48..64
+    represent .5..2, so decoded magnitudes <=12. No native GPU FP8 arithmetic.
+    Nonzero storage offset and padded physical stride are retained.
+    """
+    pitch = layout.page_bytes(page)
+    backing = torch.zeros((3, pitch + 192), device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    raw = backing[:, 64:64 + pitch]
+    if layout == KVLayout.V41:
+        values = (torch.randn(3, page * 512) * .5).clamp(-2, 2)
+        payload = values.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)
+        scale = torch.randint(124, 129, (3, page * 16), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    else:
+        payload = torch.randint(0, 256, (3, page * 256), dtype=torch.uint8)
+        scale = torch.randint(48, 65, (3, page * 32), dtype=torch.uint8)
+    raw[:, :page * layout.data_bytes].copy_(payload)
+    raw[:, layout.scale_offset(page):pitch].copy_(scale)
+    return raw
+
+
+def metrics(actual, reference):
+    a, r = actual.detach().cpu(), reference.detach().cpu()
+    delta = a.float() - r.float()

+def leaf(name):
+    spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(PACKAGE+'.'+name,SOURCE/(name+'.py'))
+    module=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[spec.name]=module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module

+KVLayout=leaf('kv_layout').KVLayout
+leaf('dequant_k_cache_sm80')

+def cache_fixture(layout,page,n=3):
+    raw=torch.randint(0,256,(n,layout.page_bytes(page)+128),dtype=torch.uint8)
+    if layout==KVLayout.V41:
+        data=raw[:,:page*512]
+        data[(data&127)==127]=0
+        # Moderate values make comparisons interpretable rather than overflow.
+        raw[:,page*512:page*528]=torch.randint(119,123,(n,page*16),dtype=torch.uint8)
+    else:
+        raw[:,page*256:page*288]=torch.randint(24,56,(n,page*32),dtype=torch.uint8)
+    return raw.cuda()
+
+
+def decode_cpu(raw,ids,page,layout):
+    c=raw.cpu();ids=ids.cpu().long()
+    pages=c[ids//page];slots=ids%page
+    data=pages.gather(1,slots[:,None]*layout.data_bytes+torch.arange(layout.data_bytes))
+    sb=pages.gather(1,layout.scale_offset(page)+slots[:,None]*layout.scale_bytes+torch.arange(layout.scale_bytes))
+    if layout==KVLayout.V41:
+        values=data.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float().double()
+        scales=sb.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu).float().double()
+    else:
+        code=torch.stack((data&15,data>>4),-1).flatten(1).long()
+        table=torch.tensor([0.,.5,1.,1.5,2.,3.,4.,6.,-0.,-.5,-1.,-1.5,-2.,-3.,-4.,-6.],dtype=torch.float64)
+        values=table[code]
+        scales=sb.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e4m3fn).float().double()
+    return (values*scales.repeat_interleave(layout.tile_size,1)).bfloat16().double()
+
+
+def reference(q,raw,indices,page,layout,scale,topk=None,sink=None,extra=None):
+    q=q.cpu().double();indices=indices.cpu()
+    out=torch.zeros_like(q);lse=torch.full(q.shape[:2],-torch.inf,dtype=torch.float64)
+    for b in range(q.shape[0]):
+        pieces=[]
+        for c,idx,p,l,lengths in [(raw,indices,page,layout,topk)]+([] if extra is None else [extra]):
+            ids=idx[b].cpu()
+            if lengths is not None:ids=ids[:max(0,int(lengths[b]))]
+            ids=ids[ids>=0]
+            if ids.numel():pieces.append(decode_cpu(c,ids,p,l))
+        if not pieces:continue
+        kv=torch.cat(pieces)
+        score=q[b]@kv.T*scale
+        lse[b]=torch.logsumexp(score,-1)
+        den=lse[b] if sink is None else torch.logaddexp(lse[b],sink.cpu().double())
+        out[b]=torch.exp(score-den[:,None])@kv
+    return out.bfloat16(),lse.float()
+

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Qualify the production SM80 selected-index sort/gather/mask/store kernel.
+
+Runtime remains opt-in. Input IDs follow torch.topk's contract: nonnegative,
+representable int32 indices; lmax <= INT_MAX and 0 <= lens <= lmax. This does
+not select top-k or change scores/ties: it only sorts already selected IDs.
+Duplicate selected IDs are deliberately retained. As in runtime reset_outputs,
+the output tail outside k is -1. No live GPU values are read by the wrapper.
+"""
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.dsv4.indexer_finish_sm80 import (
+    finish_indexer_selected_sm80 as fused_finish,
+)
+
+
+def torch_finish(idx, slots, lens, out):
+    k = idx.shape[1]
+    ids = idx.sort(dim=-1).values
+    reach = ids < lens[:, None]
+    out[:, :k] = torch.where(reach, slots.gather(1, ids.clamp_max(slots.shape[1] - 1)), -1).to(torch.int32)
+    # Runtime resets the output before write_decode; benchmark defaults k=width.
+    if k < out.shape[1]:
+        out[:, k:] = -1
+    return out
+
+
+def cpu_oracle(idx, slots, lens, width):
+    ids = idx.cpu().to(torch.int64).sort(dim=-1).values
+    slot = slots.cpu().to(torch.int64)
+    lengths = lens.cpu().to(torch.int64)
+    out = torch.full((idx.shape[0], width), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+    out[:, :idx.shape[1]] = torch.where(ids < lengths[:, None],
+        slot.gather(1, ids.clamp_max(slot.shape[1] - 1)), -1).to(torch.int32)
+    return out
+
+
+class TestFinish(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(200)
+        assert torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0), 'qualification limited to actual SM80'
+
+    def test_geometry_dtypes_duplicates_and_strides(self):
+        cases = 0
+        for bs, k, lmax in [(1, 1, 1), (1, 64, 128), (1, 127, 512),
+                             (1, 256, 32000), (1, 511, 65536),
+                             (1, 512, 65536), (3, 512, 66048)]:
+            for dtype in (torch.int32, torch.int64):
+                for strided in (False, True):
+                    factor = 2 if strided else 1
+                    idx = torch.randint(lmax, (bs, k * factor), device='cuda', dtype=dtype)[:, ::factor]
+                    if k > 3:
+                        idx[:, 1:4] = idx[:, :1]  # retain duplicate contributions
+                    slots = torch.randint(0, 2147483647, (bs, lmax * factor), device='cuda', dtype=dtype)[:, ::factor]
+                    out = torch.empty((bs, 512 * factor), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)[:, ::factor]
+                    lens = torch.empty(bs * factor, device='cuda', dtype=dtype)[::factor]
+                    for length in sorted(set([0, 1, min(511, lmax), min(512, lmax), lmax])):
+                        lens.fill_(length)
+                        reference = cpu_oracle(idx, slots, lens, 512)
+                        baseline = torch.empty_like(out)
+                        torch_finish(idx.to(torch.int64), slots, lens, baseline)
+                        self.assertTrue(torch.equal(baseline.cpu(), reference))
+                        for warps in (4, 8):
+                            out.fill_(123)
+                            fused_finish(idx, slots, lens, out, warps=warps)
+                            self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out.cpu(), reference), (bs, k, lmax, dtype, strided, length, warps))
+                            cases += 1
+        print(json.dumps({'numeric': 'exact PASS', 'geometry_cases': cases}), flush=True)
+
+    def test_graph_replay_changes_indices_slots_and_lengths(self):
+        idx = torch.randint(65536, (1, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int64)
+        slots = torch.arange(65536, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int64)[None, :] * 3
+        lens = torch.tensor([65536], device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
+        out = torch.empty((1, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
+        for warps in (4, 8):
+            for _ in range(3):
+                fused_finish(idx, slots, lens, out, warps=warps)
+            graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+            with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+                fused_finish(idx, slots, lens, out, warps=warps)
+            for length in (0, 1, 511, 512, 32000, 65536):
+                idx.copy_(torch.randint(65536, idx.shape, device='cuda', dtype=idx.dtype))
+                idx[:, :4] = 0
+                slots.add_(7)
+                lens.fill_(length)
+                out.fill_(123)
+                graph.replay()
+                self.assertTrue(torch.equal(out.cpu(), cpu_oracle(idx, slots, lens, 512)))
+        print(json.dumps({'graph_replay': 'exact PASS', 'changed_inputs': ['idx', 'slots', 'lens'], 'replays': 12}), flush=True)
+
+
+def graph_time(fn, calls, repeats):
+    # CUDA capture requires a nondefault stream. Warm and capture on exactly
+    # that stream, so Torch sort/gather temporary state is initialized there.
+    caller = torch.cuda.current_stream()
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(caller)
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    timings = []
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            fn()
+        stream.synchronize()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+            for _ in range(calls):
+                fn()
+        for _ in range(10):
+            graph.replay()
+        stream.synchronize()
+        for _ in range(repeats):
+            start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            stop = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+            start.record(stream)
+            graph.replay()
+            stop.record(stream)
+            stop.synchronize()
+            timings.append(start.elapsed_time(stop) * 1000 / calls)
+    caller.wait_stream(stream)
+    return {'median_us': statistics.median(timings), 'samples_us': timings}
+
+
+def benchmark(calls, repeats):
+    torch.manual_seed(201)
+    for lmax in (4096, 65536):
+        idx = torch.randint(lmax, (1, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int64)
+        slots = torch.randint(0, 2000000, (1, lmax), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int64)
+        lens = torch.tensor([lmax], device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
+        out = torch.empty((1, 512), device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
+        reference = cpu_oracle(idx, slots, lens, 512)
+        baseline = graph_time(lambda: torch_finish(idx, slots, lens, out), calls, repeats)
+        assert torch.equal(out.cpu(), reference)
+        for warps in (4, 8):
+            fused = graph_time(lambda: fused_finish(idx, slots, lens, out, warps=warps), calls, repeats)
+            assert torch.equal(out.cpu(), reference)
+            print(json.dumps({'benchmark': 'selected_topk_finish_only', 'device': torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
+                'shape': [1, 512], 'lmax': lmax, 'warps': warps, 'calls_per_graph': calls,
+                'baseline': baseline, 'fused': fused,
+                'speedup': baseline['median_us'] / fused['median_us'],
+                'projected_saved_ms_per_8_owners': (baseline['median_us'] - fused['median_us']) * 8 / 1000,
+                'scope': 'excludes scoring/topk/reset; local projection, not whole-model speedup'}), flush=True)
+
+
+if __name__ == '__main__':
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument('--benchmark', action='store_true')
+    parser.add_argument('--calls', type=int, default=100)
+    parser.add_argument('--repeats', type=int, default=9)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    assert torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0)
+    result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(unittest.defaultTestLoader.loadTestsFromTestCase(TestFinish))
+    if not result.wasSuccessful():
+        raise SystemExit(1)
+    if args.benchmark:
+        benchmark(args.calls, args.repeats)

+"""SM80 engram gather: GPU byte tables, independent CPU bit-format oracle.
+
+Run directly with unittest on CUDA SM80. No direct SRT imports, native FP8 views,
+experimental flags, or host-table support claims. NaN payloads are unspecified;
+all other BF16 bits (including signed zeros and infinities) must match exactly.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+from sglang.kernels.ops.embeddings.engram_gather import engram_gather
+
+
+def _is_sm80():
+    return (
+        torch.version.hip is None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0)
+    )
+
+
+def _decode_e4m3_cpu(raw):
+    """Build FP32 bits with integer significands, not a native FP8 cast."""
+    assert raw.device.type == "cpu" and raw.dtype == torch.uint8
+    table = []
+    for code in range(256):
+        sign = (code >> 7) << 31
+        exponent, fraction = (code >> 3) & 15, code & 7
+        if exponent == 15 and fraction == 7:
+            magnitude = 0x7FC00000
+        elif exponent == 0 and fraction == 0:
+            magnitude = 0
+        else:
+            # value = integer_significand * 2**power, exactly. Normalize
+            # using bit_length rather than the kernel's piecewise decoder.
+            significand = fraction if exponent == 0 else 8 + fraction
+            power = -9 if exponent == 0 else exponent - 10
+            top = significand.bit_length() - 1
+            magnitude = ((power + top + 127) << 23) | (
+                (significand - (1 << top)) << (23 - top)
+            )
+        table.append(sign | magnitude)
+    bits = torch.tensor(table, dtype=torch.int64).to(torch.int32)
+    return bits[raw.long()].contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+
+
+def _decode_ue8m0_cpu(raw):
+    """Exact FP32 bit construction, including the two boundary codes."""
+    assert raw.device.type == "cpu" and raw.dtype == torch.uint8
+    bits = raw.to(torch.int64) << 23
+    bits[raw == 0] = 0x00400000  # 2**-127, not zero
+    bits[raw == 255] = 0x7FC00000  # NaN, not infinity
+    return bits.to(torch.int32).contiguous().view(torch.float32)
+
+
+def _reference(weight, scale, ids, block_size, row_lo, row_hi):
+    assert weight.device.type == scale.device.type == ids.device.type == "cpu"
+    values = _decode_e4m3_cpu(weight)
+    scales = _decode_ue8m0_cpu(scale).repeat_interleave(block_size, dim=1)
+    # Multiply in CPU FP32 first (including overflow/underflow and 0 * NaN),
+    # then perform exactly one BF16 RNE conversion. Never use exp/exp2.
+    decoded = (values * scales).to(torch.bfloat16)
+    expected = torch.zeros(ids.numel(), weight.shape[1], dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    owned = (ids >= row_lo) & (ids < row_hi)
+    expected[owned] = decoded[(ids[owned] - row_lo).long()]
+    return expected
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(_is_sm80(), "requires CUDA SM80 (8, 0)")
+class TestEngramGatherSM80(unittest.TestCase):
+    def _assert_exact(self, actual, expected):
+        actual = actual.cpu()
+        self.assertEqual(actual.dtype, torch.bfloat16)
+        self.assertEqual(actual.shape, expected.shape)
+        # equal_nan comparison checks overflow classifications; bit comparison
+        # additionally distinguishes signed zero. Ignore only NaN payloads.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, expected, rtol=0, atol=0, equal_nan=True)
+        not_nan = ~torch.isnan(expected)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            torch.equal(
+                actual.contiguous().view(torch.int16)[not_nan],
+                expected.contiguous().view(torch.int16)[not_nan],
+            )
+        )
+
+    def _run(self, weight, scale, ids, row_lo, row_hi):
+        dim, block_size = weight.shape[1], 32
+        # Nonzero source offsets ensure the original supplied raw addresses
+        # are honored; neither allocation nor pointer is reinterpreted as FP8.
+        weight_storage = torch.full(
+            (weight.numel() + 64,), 127, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+        )
+        scale_storage = torch.full(
+            (scale.numel() + 64,), 255, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+        )
+        weight_gpu = weight_storage[32 : 32 + weight.numel()].view_as(weight)
+        scale_gpu = scale_storage[32 : 32 + scale.numel()].view_as(scale)
+        weight_gpu.copy_(weight)
+        scale_gpu.copy_(scale)
+        ids_gpu = ids.cuda()
+        out = torch.full((ids.numel(), dim), float("nan"), dtype=torch.bfloat16).cuda()
+        got = engram_gather(
+            weight_gpu.data_ptr(),
+            scale_gpu.data_ptr(),
+            ids_gpu,
+            out,
+            dim,
+            block_size,
+            row_lo,
+            row_hi,
+        )
+        self.assertIs(got, out)
+        self._assert_exact(

+def _checkpoint(n, k, group_size, *, seed, exact=False):
+    """Build checkpoint FP8 payload and E8M0 scales entirely on the CPU."""
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
+    if exact:
+        # Normal E4M3 values, exactly representable after Marlin's exponent-bias
+        # conversion. Tiny/subnormal FP8 values can round during that conversion
+        # and are deliberately not part of this zero-tolerance routing oracle.
+        values = torch.tensor([-3.0, -1.5, -0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 2.0])
+        rows = torch.arange(n).view(n, 1)
+        cols = torch.arange(k).view(1, k)
+        weight = values[(rows + 3 * cols) % values.numel()]
+        scale_rows = torch.arange(n // group_size).view(-1, 1)
+        scale_cols = torch.arange(k // group_size).view(1, -1)
+        exponents = (124 + (scale_rows + 2 * scale_cols) % 5).to(torch.uint8)
+    else:
+        weight = torch.randn(n, k, generator=generator, device="cpu") * 0.25
+        exponents = torch.randint(
+            124,
+            129,
+            (n // group_size, k // group_size),
+            generator=generator,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            device="cpu",
+        )
+    weight = weight.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).contiguous()
+    # This is the serialized UE8M0 scale representation. The block-FP8 loader
+    # destination is FP32, unlike the uint8 destination of the MXFP8 path.
+    scales = exponents.contiguous().view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu).float()
+    expanded = scales.repeat_interleave(group_size, 0).repeat_interleave(group_size, 1)
+    reference_weight = (weight.float() * expanded).contiguous()
+    return weight, scales, reference_weight
+

+def _load_marlin_functions():
+    """Exercise Python metadata/byte padding on CPU without CUDA SRT imports."""
+    source = (
+        Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]
+        / "python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/marlin_utils_fp8.py"
+    )
+    tree = ast.parse(source.read_text())
+    functions = [node for node in tree.body if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef)]
+    for node in functions:
+        node.decorator_list = []
+    namespace = {
+        "torch": torch,
+        "envs": runpy.run_path(str(source.parents[2] / "environ.py"))["envs"],
+        "Optional": __import__("typing").Optional,
+        "USE_FP32_REDUCE_DEFAULT": True,
+        "logger": SimpleNamespace(warning_once=lambda *args: None),
+    }
+    exec(  # noqa: S102 - execute only local function ASTs with controlled globals
+        compile(ast.Module(body=functions, type_ignores=[]), str(source), "exec"),
+        namespace,
+    )
+    return namespace

+"""SM80 (A100) M=1 FP8-E4M3 group-32 GEMV: contract, graph capture, Marlin wiring.
+
+Run directly with unittest (a real SM80 GPU is required):
+    python test/registered/kernels/ops/gemm/test_m1_gemv_sm80.py
+
+The kernel under test is ``sglang.kernels.ops.gemm.dsv4_m1_gemv``; the second
+class drives the production gate in ``marlin_utils_fp8`` end to end.
+
+WHAT IS CHECKED
+---------------
+The reference is the exact contract Marlin's SM80 FP8 path implements, evaluated
+in float64 on the CPU:
+
+    w_eff[n, k] = bf16( bf16(fp8_value[n, k]) * bf16(scale[n, k // 32]) )
+    out[n]      = bf16( sum_k fp64( w_eff[n, k] * x[k] ) )
+
+where ``fp8_value * 2**-120`` is rebuilt from the raw byte with the same bit
+shift the kernel uses (``((b << 8) & 0x8000) | ((b << 4) & 0x07F0)`` then a
+bf16 bitcast) and the single ``.to(bfloat16)`` is the one contract rounding.
+This is the oracle of the qualified bench
+``test/manual/layers/quantization/bench_fp8_sm80_m1_gemv.py``.
+
+Every case must satisfy the same allclose bounds that qualified bench uses
+(rtol 1.5e-2, atol 4e-3). On top of that:
+
+  * well-conditioned fixtures must land within one bf16 ulp of the largest
+    output magnitude. The kernel and the oracle associate the fp32 additions
+    differently, so "bitwise equal to the oracle" is *reported* per case rather
+    than required;
+  * fixtures whose folded product lands in the fp32 subnormal range (bf16
+    subnormal scales) are allowed the derived FTZ magnitude: every flushed term
+    is at most one bf16 step at the top of that range, so the difference is
+    bounded by K * 2**-126 * max|x|;
+  * the cancellation fixture (exact +/- weight pairs inside one 32-group, i.e.
+    an exact-zero result in real arithmetic) is judged by the qualified bounds
+    only, and reports the fp32 residual, which is the point of that fixture.
+
+A strict failure on ``subnormal_payload`` or on the codebook fixtures means the
+sm80 bf16 multiply is being promoted to fp32 with FTZ, which flushes the folded
+payload of E4M3 subnormal codes (v * 2**-120 is an fp32 subnormal for
+|v| < 2**-6). That is the one numerical mechanism this file cannot settle
+without the GPU, and it is probed deliberately instead of being tolerated.
+
+No tolerance here was chosen to make a specific number pass.

+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Exact decode mirror, float64 oracle, metrics
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _fp8_payload_to_bf16(raw: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Torch mirror of the kernel decode: fp8_value * 2**-120, bf16, bit-exact."""
+    b = raw.view(torch.uint8).to(torch.int32)
+    bits = ((b << 8) & 0x8000) | ((b << 4) & 0x07F0)
+    return bits.to(torch.int16).view(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _contract_reference(
+    w8: torch.Tensor, s: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """float64 CPU oracle of the Marlin group-32 contract.
+
+    w8: (N, K) uint8 raw E4M3; s: (N, K // 32) bf16 plain scales; x: (K,) bf16.
+    Returns (N,) bf16.
+    """
+    w8 = w8.detach().cpu()
+    s = s.detach().cpu()
+    x = x.detach().cpu()
+    n, k = w8.shape
+    ks = s.shape[1]
+    assert k == ks * GROUP, (k, ks)
+    fp8_value = _fp8_payload_to_bf16(w8).double() * float(2.0**120)
+    scale = s.double()[:, :, None].expand(n, ks, GROUP).reshape(n, k)
+    # Both operands are bf16, so the float64 product is exact and this single
+    # .to(bfloat16) is the one contract rounding.
+    w_eff = (fp8_value * scale).to(torch.bfloat16).double()
+    return (w_eff @ x.double()).to(torch.bfloat16)
+
+
+def _metrics(got: torch.Tensor, ref: torch.Tensor) -> dict:
+    got_f = got.detach().float().cpu()
+    ref_f = ref.detach().float().cpu()
+    ulp = float(ref_f.abs().max().item()) * 2.0**-8
+    return {
+        "max_abs": float((got_f - ref_f).abs().max().item()),
+        "one_bf16_ulp_at_max": ulp,
+        # -0.0 and +0.0 count as different bit patterns; this is a reported
+        # count, not a pass criterion.
+        "bitwise_equal": int(
+            (
+                got_f.to(torch.bfloat16).view(torch.int16)
+                == ref_f.to(torch.bfloat16).view(torch.int16)
+            )
+            .sum()
+            .item()
+        ),
+        "total": int(ref.numel()),
+        "qualified_allclose": bool(
+            torch.allclose(got_f, ref_f, rtol=QUALIFIED_RTOL, atol=QUALIFIED_ATOL)
+        ),
+    }

+def _codebook_weight(n: int, k: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(N, K) uint8 covering every finite E4M3 code, plus random finite bytes."""
+    flat = torch.randint(0, 256, (n * k,), generator=generator).to(torch.uint8)
+    flat[(flat & 0x7F) == 0x7F] = 0x7E
+    flat[: _FINITE_CODES.numel()] = _FINITE_CODES
+    covered = torch.unique(flat[: _FINITE_CODES.numel()]).numel()
+    assert covered == _FINITE_CODES.numel(), f"codebook coverage {covered}"
+    return flat.view(n, k).contiguous()
+
+
+def _value_weight(
+    n: int, k: int, generator: torch.Generator, spread: float = 0.25

+    """(N, K) uint8 from quantized Gaussian values."""
+    values = torch.randn(n, k, generator=generator) * spread
+    return values.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8).contiguous()
+
+
+def _subnormal_weight(n: int, k: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(N, K) uint8 drawn only from the E4M3 subnormal codes."""
+    idx = torch.randint(0, _SUBNORMAL_CODES.numel(), (n, k), generator=generator)
+    return _SUBNORMAL_CODES[idx].contiguous()

+
+def _paired_weight(n: int, k: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """(N, K) uint8 where w[:, 2i] == -w[:, 2i+1], and 2i/2i+1 share a 32-group."""
+    half = torch.randn(n, k // 2, generator=generator) * 0.25
+    w = torch.empty(n, k)
+    w[:, 0::2] = half
+    w[:, 1::2] = -half
+    converted = w.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).view(torch.uint8)
+    assert torch.equal(converted[:, 0::2], converted[:, 1::2] ^ 0x80), "pairing lost"
+    return converted.contiguous()

+    """Exact powers of two, the shape a ue8m0 block checkpoint has."""
+    exponents = torch.randint(-6, 1, (n, k // GROUP), generator=generator)
+    return torch.exp2(exponents.float()).to(torch.bfloat16)

+def _scales_general(n: int, k: int, generator: torch.Generator) -> torch.Tensor:
+    values = 0.01 + torch.rand(n, k // GROUP, generator=generator) * 1.99

+def _graph_time(call, inner: int = 20, rounds: int = 5) -> float:
+    """Median microseconds per call, CUDA-graph replayed on a non-default stream."""
+    stream = torch.cuda.Stream()
+    stream.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
+    with torch.cuda.stream(stream):
+        for _ in range(3):
+            call()
+    torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(stream)
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+    with torch.cuda.graph(graph, stream=stream):
+        for _ in range(inner):
+            call()
+    graph.replay()
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+    samples = []
+    for _ in range(rounds):
+        start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+        end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
+        start.record()
+        graph.replay()
+        end.record()
+        end.synchronize()
+        samples.append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1e3 / inner)
+    del graph
+    return statistics.median(samples)

+class M1GemvCaseMixin:
+    def check_case(
+        self,
+        name: str,
+        got: torch.Tensor,
+        ref: torch.Tensor,
+        strictness: str,
+        *,
+        k: int | None = None,
+        x_max: float | None = None,
+        extra: dict | None = None,
+    ) -> dict:
+        stats = _metrics(got, ref)
+        record = {"case": name, "strictness": strictness, **stats}
+        if strictness == "subnormal":
+            # Each flushed term is at most one bf16 step at the top of the fp32
+            # subnormal range; the accumulation is fp32, so this is the derived
+            # worst case, not a tuned constant.
+            assert k is not None and x_max is not None
+            bound = k * FP32_SUBNORMAL_BOUND * x_max
+            record["ftz_bound"] = bound
+        elif strictness == "strict":
+            bound = max(stats["one_bf16_ulp_at_max"], FP32_SUBNORMAL_BOUND)
+        else:
+            self.assertEqual(strictness, "cancellation", name)
+            bound = None
+        if bound is not None:
+            record["bound"] = bound
+        if extra:
+            record.update(extra)
+        print(json.dumps(record), flush=True)
+        message = f"{name}: {json.dumps(record)}"
+        self.assertTrue(stats["qualified_allclose"], message)
+        if bound is not None:
+            self.assertLessEqual(stats["max_abs"], bound, message)
+        return stats

+
+No runtime selection change. Run on otherwise idle SM80:
+ PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mhc_sm80_combine_norm.py --benchmark
+Baseline calls hc_combine + sgl_kernel.rmsnorm (the actual forward_cuda API,
+whose implementation appears as FlashInfer/CUTLASS RMSNorm in deployed traces).
+Fixed predeclared tolerance rtol=.015/atol=.004 on BF16 outputs; report bitwise,
+ULP, and relative RMS as well. Intermediate BF16 combine rounding is retained.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import statistics
+import sys
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+HC, H, K = 4, 5120, 20480
+EPS = 1e-6
+ATOL, RTOL = 0.004, 0.015
+
+
+def supported():
+    return (torch.version.cuda is not None and torch.version.hip is None
+            and torch.cuda.is_available() and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0))
+
+
+def functions():
+    from sgl_kernel import rmsnorm
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.mhc import hc_combine
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.hc_combine_norm import hc_combine_norm, _hc_combine_norm
+
+    def baseline(x, pre, weight):
+        return rmsnorm(hc_combine(x, pre, HC, torch.bfloat16), weight, EPS)
+
+    def fused(x, pre, weight):
+        return hc_combine_norm(x, pre, weight, EPS)
+
+    def variant(x, pre, weight, out, parts, warps):
+        _hc_combine_norm[(1, parts)](x, pre, weight, out, x.stride(0), pre.stride(0),
+                                     EPS, parts, num_warps=warps)
+        return out
+
+    return baseline, fused, variant
+
+
+def fixture(case):
+    g = torch.Generator(device='cuda').manual_seed(20200 + case)
+    x = torch.randn((1, K), generator=g, device='cuda').bfloat16()
+    pre = torch.randn((1, HC), generator=g, device='cuda') * 0.5
+    weight = (torch.randn((H,), generator=g, device='cuda') * 0.25 + 1).bfloat16()
+    mode = case % 10
+    if mode == 1:
+        x.mul_(2**-20)
+    elif mode == 2:
+        x.mul_(2**12)
+    elif mode == 3:
+        x.zero_()
+    elif mode == 4:
+        pre.copy_(torch.tensor([[8., -4., 2., -1.]], device='cuda'))
+    elif mode == 5:
+        weight.mul_(16)
+    elif mode == 6:
+        x.mul_(2**-60)  # finite/subnormal-sensitive RMS, never square overflow
+    elif mode == 7:
+        x.mul_(2**40)  # FP32 square still finite after combine
+        pre.mul_(2**-8)
+    elif mode == 8:
+        x[:, H:2*H].copy_(x[:, :H]);pre.copy_(torch.tensor([[1., -1., 0., 0.]], device='cuda'))
+    elif mode == 9:
+        weight.copy_(torch.linspace(-16, 16, H, device='cuda').bfloat16())
+        x[:, ::2].neg_()
+    return x, pre, weight
+
+
+def oracle(args):
+    x, pre, weight = [v.detach().cpu().double() for v in args]
+    x = x.reshape(1, HC, H)
+    value = torch.zeros((1, H), dtype=torch.float64)
+    for c in range(HC):
+        value = value + pre[:, c:c+1] * x[:, c]
+    # Precisely the architecture's materialized intermediate storage dtype.
+    value = value.bfloat16().double()
+    return (value / torch.sqrt(value.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + EPS) * weight).bfloat16()
+
+
+def ordered_bf16(x):
+    bits = x.contiguous().view(torch.int16).to(torch.int32)
+    return torch.where(bits < 0, -32768 - bits, bits)
+
+
+def compare(label, got, ref):
+    got, ref = got.detach().cpu(), ref.detach().cpu()
+    assert bool(torch.isfinite(got).all()) and bool(torch.isfinite(ref).all()), label
+    diff = got.float() - ref.float()
+    rms = diff.double().square().mean().sqrt()
+    ref_rms = ref.double().square().mean().sqrt().clamp_min(1e-30)
+    result = dict(comparison=label, bitwise_equal=torch.equal(got.view(torch.int16), ref.view(torch.int16)),
+                  max_abs=float(diff.abs().max()), relative_rms=float(rms/ref_rms),
+                  max_bf16_ulp=int((ordered_bf16(got)-ordered_bf16(ref)).abs().max()),
+                  atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)
+    print(json.dumps(result), flush=True)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, ref, atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)

+No production selector is changed. Run on an otherwise idle SM80 GPU:
+  PYTHONPATH=python python test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_mhc_sm80_fused_stats.py
+  ...test_mhc_sm80_fused_stats.py --benchmark
+  ...test_mhc_sm80_fused_stats.py --benchmark --rows 1 4 32
+
+The deployed V4.1 geometry is HC4, K20480, MIX24, 20 Sinkhorn iterations.
+Both configured epsilons default to 1e-6 (deepseek_v4.py config defaults).
+This path uses the existing batch-invariant tf32x3 partial projection, NOT
+mhc_pre's unrelated T2049 TileLang/TF32 path. Numerical tolerance is fixed
+before execution: atol=rtol=1e-5. Bitwise parity is reported first and can be
+required with --require-bitwise; passing numerical tests does not imply it.
+"""
+

+import argparse
+import json
+import sys
+import unittest

+import torch

+HC, K, MIX, ITERS = 4, 20480, 24, 20
+RMS_EPS, HC_EPS = 1e-6, 1e-6
+ATOL, RTOL = 1e-5, 1e-5
+REQUIRE_BITWISE = False

+
+def supported():
+    return (
+        torch.version.cuda is not None
+        and torch.version.hip is None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0)
+    )
+
+
+def functions():
+    from sglang.kernels.ops.layernorm.mhc import (
+        hc_mix_stats,
+        hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn,
+        hc_split_sinkhorn,
+    )
+
+    def unfused(x, fn, scale, base):
+        mixes = hc_mix_stats(x, fn, RMS_EPS).unsqueeze(1)
+        return tuple(
+            y.squeeze(1)
+            for y in hc_split_sinkhorn(mixes, scale, base, HC, ITERS, HC_EPS)
+        )
+
+    def fused(x, fn, scale, base):
+        return hc_mix_stats_sinkhorn(
+            x, fn, scale, base, HC, ITERS, RMS_EPS, HC_EPS
+        )
+
+    return unfused, fused

+def inputs(rows, case="signed", seed=41):
+    generator = torch.Generator(device="cuda").manual_seed(seed)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, K, generator=generator, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    fn = torch.randn(MIX, K, generator=generator, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.01
+    scale = torch.tensor([0.5, 0.25, 0.25], device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+    base = torch.randn(MIX, generator=generator, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1
+    if case == "large":
+        x.mul_(1024)
+    elif case == "tiny":
+        x.mul_(2.0**-20)
+    elif case == "zeros":
+        x.zero_()
+    elif case == "wide_coefficients":
+        scale.copy_(torch.tensor([8.0, -4.0, 12.0], device="cuda"))

+
+
+def oracle(args):
+    """Independent CPU FP64 projection, RMS, sigmoid and exact iteration count."""
+    x, fn, scale, base = [a.detach().cpu().double() for a in args]
+    mix = (x @ fn.T) / torch.sqrt(x.square().mean(-1, keepdim=True) + RMS_EPS)
+    pre = torch.sigmoid(mix[:, :HC] * scale[0] + base[:HC]) + HC_EPS
+    post = 2 * torch.sigmoid(mix[:, HC : 2 * HC] * scale[1] + base[HC : 2 * HC])
+    comb = (mix[:, 2 * HC :] * scale[2] + base[2 * HC :]).reshape(-1, HC, HC)
+    comb = torch.exp(comb - comb.amax(-1, keepdim=True))
+    comb = comb / comb.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + HC_EPS
+    comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2, keepdim=True) + HC_EPS)
+    for _ in range(ITERS - 1):
+        comb = comb / (comb.sum(-1, keepdim=True) + HC_EPS)
+        comb = comb / (comb.sum(-2, keepdim=True) + HC_EPS)
+    return pre, post, comb
+
+

+    bits = value.contiguous().view(torch.int32).to(torch.int64)
+    return torch.where(bits < 0, -(2**31) - bits, bits)
+

+        ac, bc = a.detach().cpu(), b.detach().cpu()
+        if not torch.isfinite(ac).all() or not torch.isfinite(bc).all():

+            ulp = int((ordered_fp32(ac) - ordered_fp32(bc)).abs().max())
+        error = (ac.double() - bc.double()).abs()
+        print(json.dumps({

+            "bitwise_equal": exact if bitwise_report else None,
+            "max_abs": error.max().item(), "max_fp32_ulp": ulp,
+            "atol": ATOL, "rtol": RTOL,
+        }), flush=True)
+        if bitwise_report and REQUIRE_BITWISE and not exact:
+            raise AssertionError(f"{label}/{name}: strict bitwise qualification failed")
+        torch.testing.assert_close(ac.double(), bc.double(), atol=ATOL, rtol=RTOL)

+            reference = oracle(args)

+

+Run with ``python test_mhc_sm80_v41.py`` (or pytest). No server, checkpoint,
+process group, or initialized runtime context is needed. CPU selector tests AST-

+module and retain every TileLang kernel, including its warnings/race checker.

+import inspect
+import unittest

+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace

+from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

+import torch

+_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[5]

+HC, H, MIX, K = 4, 5120, 24, 20480
+EPS, SINKHORN_ITERS = 1e-6, 20

+def _load_functions(*names):
+    """AST isolation avoids importing distributed/model providers on CPU.
+
+    Extract function bodies verbatim, not a copied selector or reimplementation.
+    This also exposes the existing Torch oracle without a private-symbol import.
+    """
+    tree = ast.parse(_SOURCE.read_text(), filename=str(_SOURCE))
+    nodes = [
+        node
+        for node in tree.body
+        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in names
+    ]
+    if {node.name for node in nodes} != set(names):
+        raise AssertionError(f"mHC source no longer defines {names}")
+    namespace = {"torch": torch, "Tuple": Tuple}
+    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(_SOURCE), "exec"), namespace)
+    return SimpleNamespace(**namespace)
+

+    return (
+        torch.version.hip is None
+        and torch.cuda.is_available()
+        and torch.cuda.get_device_capability() == (8, 0)
+    )

+def _standalone_context(module):
+    """Mock runtime plumbing only; never replace a GPU compute kernel."""
+    stack = ExitStack()
+    for name, replacement in {
+        "get_parallel": lambda: SimpleNamespace(tp_group=None),
+        "use_symmetric_memory": lambda *args, **kwargs: nullcontext(),
+        "is_allocation_symmetric": lambda: False,
+        "_use_deep_gemm_hc_prenorm": lambda: False,
+    }.items():

+"""Regress SM80 stream device ownership and reduction architecture isolation.
+
+Run detached repository function ASTs so these policy regressions need no CUDA
+installation. Kernels are not replaced in numerical tests; this suite only checks
+resource ownership and dispatch contracts.
+"""

+import ast

+def load_function(path, name, namespace):
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+    node = next(n for n in tree.body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
+    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=[node], type_ignores=[]), str(path), "exec"), namespace)
+    return namespace[name]
+
+
+class TestSM80ResourcePolicy(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_streams_follow_device_capture_and_context_reset(self):
+        """A second device must not inherit the first device's CUDA stream."""
+        resources = NS(streams={})
+        state = NS(capturing=False)
+        cuda = NS(
+            current_device=lambda: 0,
+            is_current_stream_capturing=lambda: state.capturing,
+            Stream=lambda device: NS(device=device),
+        )
+        torch = NS(cuda=cuda, device=lambda value: NS(index=int(value.split(":")[1])))
+        path = ROOT / "python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/sparse_attention_sm80_tiled.py"
+        get_stream = load_function(
+            path, "_partial_side_stream", {"torch": torch, "_PARTIAL_SIDE_STREAM": None}
+        )
+        runtime = NS(get_resources=lambda: resources)
+        with patch.dict(sys.modules, {"sglang.srt.runtime_context": runtime}):
+            first = get_stream("cuda:0")
+            second = get_stream("cuda:1")
+            self.assertIsNot(first, second)
+            self.assertEqual(first.device.index, 0)
+            self.assertEqual(second.device.index, 1)
+            state.capturing = True
+            self.assertIs(get_stream("cuda:0"), first)
+            self.assertIsNone(get_stream("cuda:2"))
+            resources.streams.clear()  # reset_context installs a fresh resource tier.
+            self.assertIsNone(get_stream("cuda:0"))
+            state.capturing = False
+            self.assertIsNot(get_stream("cuda:0"), first)
+
+    def test_tiled_decode_stays_opt_in_and_rejects_junk_thresholds(self):

+            )

+def _load_functions(path, names, namespace):
+    source = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+    functions = [
+        node
+        for node in source.body
+        if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name in names
+    ]
+    if len(functions) != len(names):
+        raise AssertionError(f"Missing production functions: {names}")
+    future = ast.ImportFrom(
+        module="__future__", names=[ast.alias(name="annotations")], level=0
+    )
+    isolated = ast.fix_missing_locations(
+        ast.Module(body=[future, *functions], type_ignores=[])
+    )
+    exec(compile(isolated, str(path), "exec"), namespace)  # noqa: S102

+def load(path, name, namespace, cls=None, remove_imports=False):
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+    nodes = tree.body
+    if cls:
+        nodes = next(
+            n.body for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.ClassDef) and n.name == cls
+        )
+    node = next(n for n in nodes if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
+    if remove_imports:

+            (self.tensor(), self.tensor(shape=(2,), dtype="i64"), None),

+        for args in signatures:

+        self.assertEqual(len(g._cache), len(signatures))
+        self.assertEqual(self.rt.events.count("capture_enter"), len(signatures))

+    def test_capture_failure_is_fatal_and_poisoned_not_eager(self):
+        g = self.cls("deepseek_v41")

+            return self.rt.fn(h, ids, global_ids)

+        calls = self.rt.calls
+        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "previously failed"):

+        self.assertEqual(self.rt.calls, calls)
+        self.assertNotIn("replay", self.rt.events)

+"""CPU torch regressions for exact SM80 selection; no runtime/CUDA imports."""

+register_cpu_ci = runpy.run_path(

+class PrefillInputs(NS):

+            self.out_page_indices.fill_(-1)
+
+
+class DecodeInputs(NS):
+    def reset_outputs(self):

+class Struct:
+    def __init_subclass__(cls, **kwargs):
+        super().__init_subclass__()
+
+    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
+        self.__dict__.update(kwargs)

+
+def extract(path, names, namespace):
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+    nodes = [n for n in tree.body if getattr(n, "name", None) in names]
+    module = ast.Module(
+        body=[
+            ast.ImportFrom(
+                module="__future__", names=[ast.alias(name="annotations")], level=0
+            ),
+            *nodes,
+        ],
+        type_ignores=[],
+    )
+    exec(compile(ast.fix_missing_locations(module), str(path), "exec"), namespace)  # noqa: S102
+
+
+def namespace():
+    ns = dict(
+        torch=torch,
+        envs=ENVS,
+        F=F,
+        PrefillInputs=PrefillInputs,
+        DecodeInputs=DecodeInputs,
+        CandidateMetadata=type("CandidateMetadata", (), {}),
+        msgspec=NS(Struct=Struct),
+    )
+    helper = ROOT / "python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/sm80_utils.py"
+    gate_ns = dict(
+        envs=ENVS,
+        torch=NS(
+            device=lambda d: NS(type="cuda"),
+            version=NS(hip=None),
+            cuda=NS(is_available=lambda: True, get_device_capability=lambda d: (8, 0)),
+        ),
+    )
+    extract(helper, {"is_dsv41_sm80_experimental"}, gate_ns)
+    ns["is_dsv41_sm80_experimental"] = gate_ns["is_dsv41_sm80_experimental"]
+    ns["is_deep_select_supported"] = lambda: False
+    # Execute original baseline torch scoring/writes with CPU-only dependencies.
+    ns["_TORCH_SCORE_BUDGET_BYTES"] = 1024
+    extract(
+        BASE / "scoring.py",
+        {
+            "RequestScores",
+            "ChunkScores",
+            "DecodeScores",
+            "prefill_requests",
+            "_score_chunks",
+            "write_prefill",
+            "write_decode",
+        },
+        ns,
+    )
+    extract(
+        ROOT / "python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/dsv4/candidate_blocks.py",
+        {"select_candidate_block_ids", "topk_among_blocks"},
+        ns,
+    )
+    extract(
+        BASE / "full_topk.py",
+        {"_all_causal_bound", "_write_all_causal", "FullTopKIndexer"},
+        ns,
+    )
+    extract(BASE / "dense_blocks.py", {"BlockIds", "DenseBlocksBackend"}, ns)
+    extract(BASE / "types.py", {"get_tail_row_indices"}, ns)
+    ns["async_h2d"] = lambda values, dtype, device: torch.tensor(
+        values, dtype=dtype, device=device
+    )
+    return ns, gate_ns
+
+
+def inputs(ratio=1, lengths=(512, 31), rows=(4, 3), pages=True):
+    positions = torch.cat([torch.arange(s - n, s) for s, n in zip(lengths, rows)])
+    req_rows = torch.cat(
+        [torch.full((n,), r, dtype=torch.long) for r, n in enumerate(rows)]
+    )
+    indexer = NS(
+        index_topk=512, scores=Mock(side_effect=AssertionError("shortcut scored"))
+    )
+    return PrefillInputs(
+        indexer=indexer,
+        positions=positions,
+        req_rows=req_rows,
+        req_pool_indices=torch.arange(len(rows)),
+        compress_ratio=ratio,
+        seq_lens_cpu=list(lengths),
+        rows_per_request=list(rows),
+        layer_id=0,
+        x=torch.zeros(len(positions), 1),
+        q_lora=torch.zeros(len(positions), 1),
+        freqs_cis=torch.zeros(max(lengths, default=0), 1),
+        out_raw_indices=torch.full((len(positions), 512), 99, dtype=torch.int32),
+        out_page_indices=torch.full((len(positions), 512), 99, dtype=torch.int32)
+        if pages
+        else None,
+    )
+
+
+def request_map(width=17000):
+    # Disjoint non-contiguous physical slots for two requests; ratio-2 aligned.
+    return torch.stack(
+        [torch.arange(width) * 6 + 1000, torch.arange(width) * 10 + 200000]
+    )
+
+
+def enable_baseline(i):
+    i.indexer.queries = lambda q, f: torch.zeros(len(q), 1, 1)
+    i.indexer.head_weights = lambda x: torch.zeros(len(x), 1)
+    i.indexer.scores = Mock(
+        side_effect=lambda q, k, w: torch.arange(len(k), dtype=torch.float32)[
+            None, :
+        ].expand(len(q), -1)
+    )
+    return NS(
+        get_low_ratio_index_k_dequant=lambda layer, slots: torch.zeros(len(slots), 1)
+    )

+    def assert_expected(self, i):

+        ):

+            raw = torch.full((512,), -1, dtype=torch.int32)
+            raw[:n] = torch.arange(n)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(i.out_raw_indices[row], raw)
+            if i.out_page_indices is not None:
+                slots = torch.full_like(raw, -1)
+                slots[:n] = (
+                    self.mapping[req, torch.arange(n) * i.compress_ratio]
+                    // i.compress_ratio

+                torch.testing.assert_close(i.out_page_indices[row], slots)

+    def test_prefill_prefix_chunks_ratios_and_zero(self):

+    def test_whole_batch_wide_missing_metadata_and_gates_fallback(self):
